clue.text: Face Cockney's feverish disputation by logic

parts.note: a clock or watch face is its dial

indicators.note: a Cockney speaker drops the aitch at the start of a word

parts.note: hectic means feverish, flushed and excited

explanation.surface: Someone argues heatedly, face flushed, in a London accent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cockney's' takes the H off HECTIC, leaving ECTIC, as a Cockney would drop it.
explanation.definitionFit: Dialectic is the art of reaching truth through reasoned debate between opposing views.

clue.text: Cowardly in war like young Lochinvar's rival in love

definitions.text: in war like young Lochinvar's rival in love
definitions.meaning: in Scott's ballad Lochinvar's rival for Ellen is 'a laggard in love, and a dastard in war'

explanation.surface: A coward in battle is likened to the feeble suitor in a famous romantic ballad.
explanation.walkthrough: Young Lochinvar is a ballad in Walter Scott's poem Marmion; the rival is described there as a dastard in war, which this clue echoes.
explanation.definitionFit: Dastardly means craven and mean-spirited, the conduct of a dastard or base coward.

clue.text: A judicial examination unfinished in Roman courts

indicators.note: unfinished means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a trial is the examination of a case before a judge

explanation.surface: A court case is left incomplete in the law courts of ancient Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfinished' drops the L of TRIAL, leaving TRIA.
explanation.definitionFit: An atrium was the central courtyard hall of a Roman house; these are the plural.

clue.text: Gee-up with oil processing — a dramatic ending

indicators.note: processing means the letters are worked over into a new form

explanation.surface: A rider shouts to the horse while oil is being refined, reaching a theatrical climax.
explanation.walkthrough: 'processing' rearranges the letters of GEEUP and OIL together.
explanation.definitionFit: An epilogue is a closing speech or section that concludes a play.

clue.text: Transgression creates very outlandish and critical position

parts.note: French, a foreign or outlandish tongue, says tres for very
a pass is a critical state of affairs, as in 'things have come to a pretty pass'

explanation.surface: Wrongdoing leads to a very strange and dangerous predicament.
explanation.definitionFit: A trespass is a sin or offence, as in the Lord's Prayer's 'forgive us our trespasses'.

clue.text: Where one practises a vice in, company with gamblers

definitions.text: Where one practises a vice in, company with gamblers

indicators.note: in places A SIN inside the company abbreviation

parts.note: a vice is a sin

explanation.surface: A place where people go to indulge their vices in the company of gamblers.
explanation.walkthrough: The comma after 'in' is surface punctuation; read as a whole, the clue also describes a gambling house, so it doubles as its own definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A casino is a gambling establishment where people wager on games of chance.

clue.text: Pot plant

definitions.meaning: a green herbage plant of lawns and meadows

explanation.definitionFit: Grass is slang for marijuana and also the ordinary green herbage of fields.

clue.text: Oriental show-girl of the nineties

parts.note: a Japanese hostess trained to entertain, and also the title of a hit London musical comedy of 1896

explanation.surface: A Japanese entertainer from a Victorian stage show.
explanation.walkthrough: The Geisha was a popular musical comedy that opened in London in 1896, so the clue works both as a description of the hostess and of the show.
explanation.definitionFit: A geisha is a Japanese woman trained in music and dance to entertain guests.

clue.text: King George, say, in stone or concrete material

indicators.note: in places the royal cipher and the example inside the stone

parts.note: agate is a banded semi-precious stone
GR stands for Georgius Rex, King George
say means for example, abbreviated EG

explanation.surface: A monarch is commemorated in stone or in concrete.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' as EG and GR, the royal cipher of a King George, are crossword staples; aggregate here is the builders' sense, not a total.
explanation.definitionFit: Aggregate is the sand, gravel or crushed rock mixed with cement to make concrete.

clue.text: Smooth and shiny — for sailors it's bottoms up!

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: keels are the bottoms of ships, as sailors know

explanation.surface: A glossy finish described with the drinking toast 'bottoms up' in naval slang.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reads KEELS from the bottom, giving the answer; 'bottoms up' is also a drinking toast.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleek describes a surface that is glossy and well groomed, like a cat's coat.

clue.text: Could be an ace writer of sourdough's songs

definitions.meaning: in tennis a serve that the opponent cannot touch is an ace
Robert W. ... wrote Songs of a Sourdough, poems of the Yukon gold rush

explanation.definitionFit: A tennis serve can be an ace, and the poet Robert Service wrote verse about Klondike prospectors, called sourdoughs.

clue.text: Hair style seen at the seaside

definitions.meaning: a short tapered bob cut fashionable in the 1920s

explanation.definitionFit: A shingle was a cropped 1920s women's haircut, and shingle is the pebbly gravel covering many beaches.

clue.text: Where Davy Crockett fought Mexicans Missouri fashion

parts.note: a la means in the fashion of
MO is the postal abbreviation for the state of Missouri

explanation.surface: A frontier hero battles Mexican troops in the manner of a Midwestern state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Missouri fashion' reads as 'a la MO', in Missouri style.
explanation.definitionFit: The Alamo was the San Antonio mission besieged in 1836, where Crockett died defending it against Santa Anna's army.

clue.text: Counterfeit gold Mr Pecksniff's Tom found by a stream

parts.note: Tom Pinch is the loyal assistant of Mr Pecksniff in Dickens's Martin Chuzzlewit
a beck is a northern English word for a brook

explanation.surface: A Dickens character comes across fake gold beside a brook.
explanation.definitionFit: Pinchbeck is a copper-zinc alloy made to imitate gold, hence anything sham or tawdry.

clue.text: Concealment of identity of underworld Runyon types, say

parts.note: Dis is the Roman god and realm of the underworld

indicators.note: say signals that the word is to be spoken, giving a sound-alike

parts.note: Damon Runyon wrote the stories behind Guys and Dolls, full of Broadway guys

explanation.surface: Gangsters from Runyon's stories hide who they really are.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' turns GUYS into its sound-alike GUISE.
explanation.definitionFit: A disguise is a costume or change of appearance used to hide who one is.

clue.text: Second circuits of course take credit for this comedy

parts.note: laps are circuits of a racecourse
tick is British slang for credit, as in buying on tick

explanation.surface: Racers on their second time round the track get credit for a farce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On tick' is British slang for buying something on credit.
explanation.definitionFit: Slapstick is boisterous physical comedy of pratfalls and custard pies.

clue.text: Froth, or where it is blown by many

parts.note: froth on beer is blown off at the bar of a pub
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, so many

explanation.surface: Foam on beer, and the pub counter where drinkers blow it off.
explanation.walkthrough: M, a thousand, often stands for 'many' in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: Barm is the frothy yeast that forms on fermenting malt liquor.

clue.text: Not a theme' that's terribly antiquated

indicators.note: terribly suggests the letters are badly mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: A writer dismisses a hackneyed subject as hopelessly dated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terribly' rearranges NOT A THEME.
explanation.definitionFit: Something moth-eaten is old and shabby, like cloth chewed by moth larvae, hence outdated.

clue.text: On first of May musical instrument is something alive

indicators.note: on in a down clue means placed above, so these come before the initial

parts.note: the organ is a keyboard instrument with pipes

indicators.note: first of takes the opening letter of the following word

explanation.surface: An instrument plays on May Day as spring comes to life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' places ORGAN IS above M, the first of May, in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: An organism is any living thing, plant, animal or microbe.

clue.text: Wrong to square a magistrate in Rome

indicators.note: wrong means the letters are set out in the wrong order

explanation.surface: Someone thinks it would be wrong to bribe a Roman official.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wrong' rearranges TO SQUARE.
explanation.definitionFit: A quaestor was a Roman official in charge of public finances and treasury.

clue.text: Time of world revolution

parts.note: not a political upheaval but the period the Earth takes to circle the sun once

explanation.surface: A period of global political upheaval.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolution' suggests overthrow, but here it is the Earth's orbit.
explanation.definitionFit: A year is the time the Earth takes to complete one orbit of the sun.

clue.text: 1 ac heard by young Omar from doctor and saint

definitions.meaning: a cross-reference to the clue at 1 across, a reasoned disputation

definitions.text: heard by young Omar from doctor and saint
definitions.meaning: in FitzGerald's Rubaiyat Omar says that when young he did frequent Doctor and Saint and heard great discussion about it and about

explanation.definitionFit: Dialectic is reasoned debate, and FitzGerald's Omar Khayyam heard great debate from doctors and saints in his youth.

clue.text: Recipient of helping is without a sense of taste

definitions.text: Recipient of helping is without a sense of taste

parts.words: Recipient of helping is without a sense of taste
parts.note: the roof of the mouth receives each helping of food, yet the clue pretends it lacks any sense of taste

explanation.surface: Someone served a portion of food cannot taste it.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue plays on the organ both receiving the food and being the seat of taste.
explanation.definitionFit: The palate is the roof of the mouth, onto which food goes, and also means the sense of taste.

clue.text: A fellow is killed by a boar

definitions.text: A fellow is killed by a boar

parts.note: a don is a fellow or tutor of a college

explanation.surface: A college fellow meets his end at the tusks of a wild pig.
explanation.walkthrough: In Greek myth the beautiful youth beloved of Aphrodite was gored to death by a wild boar.
explanation.definitionFit: Adonis was the handsome youth of myth killed by a boar while hunting.

clue.text: Like George in car crash disaster she foretold

indicators.note: in places the novelist phrase inside the wrecked letters
crash signals that the letters of car are smashed up

parts.note: as means like
George Sand was the pen name of the French novelist Aurore Dupin

explanation.surface: A prophet foresaw a car crash, like the novelist did.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crash' scrambles the car; 'Like George' means 'as Sand', after the French novelist George Sand. Cassandra was also the pen name of a famous Daily Mirror columnist.
explanation.definitionFit: Cassandra was the Trojan prophetess fated to foresee calamity and never be believed.

clue.text: Nag of Kipling's in the horse artillery

parts.note: a cob is a sturdy short-legged horse
RA is the Royal Artillery

explanation.surface: An old horse from a Kipling story serves with the mounted gunners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nag' looks like a horse, but Nag is the snake in Kipling's Rikki-Tikki-Tavi.
explanation.definitionFit: In The Jungle Book story the mongoose Rikki-Tikki-Tavi fights Nag, a big black serpent.

clue.text: It's a bore, we agree in this

indicators.note: in signals that the letters sit inside the phrase we agree

explanation.surface: People agree that something is tedious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bore' is the tidal wave on a river, not a tedious person.
explanation.definitionFit: An eagre is a tidal bore, a wave surging up an estuary such as the Severn or Trent.

clue.text: Butter about right for fourpence once

indicators.note: about means the first word goes around the second

parts.note: a goat is something that butts

explanation.surface: Butter costing a few old pennies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Butter' is not the dairy spread but one who butts; 'about' puts GOAT around R.
explanation.definitionFit: A groat was an old English silver coin worth four pennies.

clue.text: Man of high IQ holds it for the country

indicators.note: holds means the first word wraps around the second

parts.note: a brain is a very clever person

explanation.surface: A genius holds a position on behalf of his nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man of high IQ' looks like a person in the surface, but it is simply a crossword's way of saying a clever brain.
explanation.definitionFit: Britain is the island nation comprising England, Scotland and Wales.

clue.text: Anthem includes in it one torn in pieces

indicators.note: includes in it means the two letters wrap round what follows
in pieces means the letters are broken up and reassembled

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A hymn includes a phrase about a man torn apart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in pieces' rearranges one (I) with TORN, giving NTROI; 'includes in' means the little word it wraps around that jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: An introit is a psalm or anthem sung as the priest approaches the altar at the start of Mass.

clue.text: To be brilliant this steeplechaser has odds on at first

indicators.note: on at first means the odds abbreviation stands at the front, so removing it leaves the rest

parts.note: to sparkle is to be brilliant
SP is starting price, the odds in a horse race

explanation.surface: A racehorse is tipped to shine, with short odds offered.
explanation.walkthrough: SP plus the horse's name makes SPARKLE; Arkle was a legendary Irish steeplechaser of the 1960s.
explanation.definitionFit: Arkle was a celebrated Irish racehorse who won three Cheltenham Gold Cups.

clue.text: Goodfellow as neighbour to one that fell among thieves

definitions.text: Goodfellow as neighbour to one that fell among thieves

parts.words: Goodfellow as neighbour to one that fell among thieves
parts.note: recalls the parable of the traveller robbed on the Jericho road and the stranger who helped him

explanation.surface: A kindly man proves a true neighbour to a mugging victim.
explanation.walkthrough: In Luke's gospel Jesus asks who was neighbour to the man who fell among thieves; the answer is the one who showed mercy.
explanation.definitionFit: A Samaritan, after the parable, is anyone who helps a stranger in need.
